strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Intermediate Buffers
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with element-wise scale/unscale between each stage, using explicit buffer clones and loops over world_size shards. Results in 8 all-reduce dispatches plus 14 local compute kernels (7 scale + 7 unscale loops). Minimizes algorithmic complexity at the cost of maximum dispatch count.

strategies.name: Fused Local Operations Between All-Reduces
strategies.desc: Merges the scale and unscale operations into single vectorized kernels that process all shards in one pass, eliminating intermediate loops. Maintains 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local compute to 7 fused kernels (one scale-unscale fusion per stage except the first). Trades code complexity for fewer local dispatches while keeping collective count constant.

strategies.name: Precomputed Scale Tensor Broadcasting
strategies.desc: Precomputes a [W, S] scale tensor once, then uses tensor broadcasting/multiplication to apply per-shard scales without explicit loops over world_size. Requires 8 all-reduce dispatches but replaces 14 loop-based operations with 7 broadcast multiplications. Better memory access patterns and potential hardware acceleration of broadcast ops.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing overlap of the scale/unscale computation during the gather phase. Results in 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but enables pipelining of local ops with communication. Trades increased collective count for potential latency hiding through computation-communication overlap.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc:
Exploits potential node structure by performing intra-node all-reduce followed by inter-node all-reduce at each stage, applying scales only at node boundaries. Requires 16 collective dispatches (8 intra-node + 8 inter-node AR) but reduces scale operation granularity and may leverage faster intra-node interconnect. Optimal when num_nodes > 1 and nodes have balanced rank distribution.
